title: Review gate
summary: A reviewer reads your branch and reports bugs. Every finding must quote real code, gets fixed once, and is logged.

explain.what: The review gate is a code-review skill plus a small shared script (review.mjs). When you ask your agent to review a branch, the script asks a model from your reviewer role in ACS (Models → Roles) to read the committed changes and report bugs. Each finding must quote the exact code it is about, and a script checks that quote before you ever see the finding. The optional parts add an agent guard, a push gate and Codex log access.
explain.does: Day to day you say /code-review (or 'review this branch') for bugs, /security-check for security holes alone, and /pr-review when a branch is ready for its pull request: it runs the code review and, when the security setting is on, the security pass in one review, then the fixes, a context pass that brings comments and docs in line with the code, the push and the description. The script picks a reviewer from your reviewer role, skipping any whose CLI you have not installed and saying which it skipped. It writes a report under reviews/ in the repo and one line to a review log. You decide which findings to fix; fixes are recorded with a close, and disputed findings can get a second model's verdict. If no reviewer can run, it stops and tells you exactly what to fix (install model-id, set the reviewer role, or install a CLI). It never quietly uses a model your role does not list.
changes: ~/.claude/skills/ and ~/.codex/skills/: code-review, security-check, pr-review and context-pass (the skills, for the CLIs you have)
~/.agent-config-studio/review-gate/ (the shared script, the scoring calibration and an example config)
~/.agent-config-studio/review-log/review-log.jsonl (created by your first review)
anything an optional part lists, only if you turn that part on
~/.agent-config-studio/roles.json, only for the reviewer role you choose at install if not set yet (no model is set for you; kept after uninstall)
explain.undo: Uninstalling removes the skill folders and, once no installed part uses it, the shared ~/.agent-config-studio/review-gate/ folder. A file you edited after installing is kept and reported. Your review log and the reports in each repo's reviews/ folder are your history and are never deleted.

workflow.note: /code-review and /security-check also run on their own; neither counts as a PR review alone. After the push, /pr writes the description.

parts.title: Review-gate rules in your global instructions

explain.what: A short, marked block of rules for your agents: where the review script lives, that only the operator waives findings or overrides the gate, and that every PR body lists its Deferred findings.
explain.does: Your agents read these rules in every session, so they run reviews the same way in every project without you repeating them.
changes: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: one marked block added (the rest of the file is untouched)
~/.codex/AGENTS.md: one marked block added (the rest of the file is untouched)
explain.undo: Uninstalling removes only the marked block; everything else in those files, including ACS's own model-guide block, stays as it was.

explain.what: A hook your agents' shell commands pass through before they run. It refuses commands that would skip or switch off the review gate: git push or commit with --no-verify or -n, changing core.hooksPath, changing any reviewgate.* git setting, and git send-pack.
explain.does: When an agent tries one of those commands, the command is blocked with a one-line reason and the agent has to get its change reviewed instead. Everything else runs as normal. It is an accident barrier for agents, not a security boundary, and it never touches commands you type in your own terminal.
changes: ~/.claude/settings.json: PreToolUse hooks for Bash and Monitor that run the guard (only if ~/.claude exists)
hooks.json in each Codex home: a PreToolUse hook for Bash (~/.codex if it exists, $CODEX_HOME, and any codexHomes listed in ~/.agent-config-studio/review-gate/config.json)
config.toml in each Codex home: a marked trust block (# review-gate agent guard begin … # end) so Codex runs the hook
~/.agent-config-studio/review-gate/hooks/agent-guard, agent-guard.mjs and node-path (the guard and the node it runs on)
~/.agent-config-studio/review-gate-agent-guard.json (what was installed, for a clean uninstall)
~/.agent-config-studio/backups/review-gate-guard-<time>/ (a copy of every file before it changed)
explain.undo: Uninstalling removes only the guard's own hook entries and trust block. A file that has not changed since install gets its exact earlier bytes back; a file you edited keeps your edits and loses only the guard's entries. CLIs that are not installed are skipped.

parts.title: Push gate for repos you opt in

explain.what: A git pre-push check that refuses to push code no review has closed. To reach every repo, it sets your global git core.hooksPath, so every repo's git hooks go through a pass-through. A repo's own .git/hooks still run, exactly as before, except a push-to-checkout hook (see the changes). A repo that sets its own core.hooksPath (Husky and similar tools) bypasses the pass-through, so it is not gated. The review check itself applies only to repos you opt in with git config reviewgate.enabled true.
explain.does: In an opted-in repo, git push is refused until a review of those commits is closed, and the refusal names the first unreviewed commit. A reviewed push goes through and prints the review summary for your PR. Pushes in every other repo behave exactly as they did. If node is missing, an opted-in repo's push is refused rather than let through unchecked.
changes: your global git config (~/.gitconfig, or $GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL): core.hooksPath = ~/.agent-config-studio/review-gate/hooks/global
~/.agent-config-studio/review-gate/hooks/ (the pass-through hooks, the gate and node-path, the node they run on)
~/.agent-config-studio/review-gate-global-hook.json (your previous core.hooksPath, for uninstall)
each repo you opt in: reviewgate.enabled = true in that repo's .git/config (you choose which repos)

any repo with its own .git/hooks/push-to-checkout: that hook will not run while the global hooks are on. The pass-through leaves push-to-checkout out on purpose, so a push into a checked-out branch keeps git's own receive.denyCurrentBranch = updateInstead behavior. Install and status name each repo that has one.
explain.undo: Uninstalling restores your previous core.hooksPath: the exact earlier bytes of your global git config when nothing else changed, otherwise only the core.hooksPath line. A reviewgate.enabled setting you added to a repo stays until you remove it with git config --unset reviewgate.enabled.

explain.what: An extra opt-in for the push gate: every repo that is a worktree project (one of its worktrees has a .worktrees.conf, as the worktree setup creates) is gated too, without opting each repo in by hand.
explain.does: Pushes from any worktree of such a project need a closed review, like an opted-in repo. Other repos are not affected. It needs the push gate part.
changes: your global git config: reviewgate.worktreeProjects = true
explain.undo: Uninstalling removes that one setting from your global git config.

explain.what: Codex runs commands in a sandbox that can only write inside the project. This part lets a review started from Codex write the shared review log.
explain.does: Reviews, disputes and closes run from a Codex session can record themselves in ~/.agent-config-studio/review-log/ instead of failing to write the log.
changes: config.toml in each Codex home: ~/.agent-config-studio/review-log added to writable_roots under [sandbox_workspace_write]
~/.agent-config-studio/backups/ (a copy of each config.toml before it changed)
explain.undo: Uninstalling removes only that one writable_roots entry. If config.toml has not changed since install, its exact earlier bytes come back.
